dynamic_exports.edge: The package containing the table points to each statically resolved owner module.
dynamic_exports.other_protocols: __all__, ordinary assignments, __getattr__ bodies, and generic dynamic-import calls do not create string edges.
dynamic_exports.symbol_multiplicity: Multiple exported symbols owned by one module produce one edge.
dynamic_exports.unresolved_values: Non-literal owners produce no edge and are not guessed.

edge_direction: The source module points to the module it may depend on at runtime.

all_or_assignment_reexport.reason: __all__ names symbols rather than owner modules, and an assignment does not add a module dependency beyond the expression that produced its value. Inferring owners from names would be guesswork.
all_or_assignment_reexport.rule: Do not create an edge from __all__ strings or ordinary assignment-based re-exports. Their underlying AST import, when present, remains an edge.

ast_delayed_import.reason: A delayed import does not create an eager import cycle, but calling the function can execute it. The graph measures possible runtime architecture dependencies, so excluding it would hide real coupling.
ast_delayed_import.rule: Collect the same Import and ImportFrom forms inside function or async-function bodies and mark them as delayed edges.

ast_eager_import.reason: These statements declare direct, statically reproducible runtime dependencies.
ast_eager_import.resolution: Import uses the exact imported module when it is a node. ImportFrom uses the resolved module operand; for from . import x, it also uses each named child module that is a node. Star imports point to the resolved module operand. Aliases do not change the target.
ast_eager_import.rule: Collect Import and ImportFrom statements outside function and async-function bodies, including class bodies and both potentially executable conditional branches.

generic_dynamic_import.reason: Targets can depend on runtime values. Partially evaluating selected call expressions would create an unstable, incomplete graph; a new governed dynamic table requires a new definition version.
generic_dynamic_import.rule: Do not infer edges from importlib.import_module, __import__, loader APIs, computed strings, or plugin-like registries other than the explicit _EXPORTS rule.

lazy_export_owner.reason: The table is an executable lazy import dispatch contract. Attribute access can import its owner even though no Import AST node names that owner.
lazy_export_owner.rule: In package __init__.py modules only, collect statically resolvable owner module strings from literal _EXPORTS dictionary values and _EXPORTS[...] assignments. Resolve relative owner strings against that package. Deduplicate symbols that share an owner.

package_parent.reason: Python initializes a package before loading its child module. Keeping this as a separate edge kind makes its large SCC effect visible rather than silently folding it into AST resolution.
package_parent.rule: For every non-root module node, add an edge to its immediate dotted parent when that parent is also a node.

type_checking_import.reason: TYPE_CHECKING is false in normal runtime execution, so these are type dependencies rather than possible runtime dependencies.
type_checking_import.rule: Exclude imports in branches proven unreachable at runtime from TYPE_CHECKING or typing.TYPE_CHECKING tests; include the runtime branch of a negated test. Unknown conditions retain both branches.

purpose: Measure possible runtime module dependencies for architecture review; this is not an eager-import deadlock detector or a domain ownership classifier.

scc.algorithm: Tarjan strongly connected components with nodes and outgoing targets visited in lexical order.
scc.all_singletons: A one-node component is an SCC in the algorithmic partition.
scc.cycle: A component is reported as cyclic when it has more than one node, or when its single node has an explicit self-edge.
scc.ordering: Reported cyclic components sort by descending size and then lexical member list. Members sort lexically.
scc.self_loop: A singleton with an explicit self-edge counts as a cyclic SCC.
scc.singleton_without_self_loop: A singleton without a self-edge does not count as a cycle or a non-trivial SCC.

scope.excluded: Non-Python files, directories without a .py file of their own, tests, scripts, generated cache files, and dependencies outside gravity_insight are not nodes.
scope.node: Every .py file recursively below package_root is one module node.
scope.ordinary_module: Any other .py file maps to its dotted import name relative to package_root.
scope.package_init: A package __init__.py is the package module node itself; for example gravity_insight/agents/__init__.py is gravity_insight.agents.
